Bassist Bob Haggart was one of the swing era’s most notable instrumentalists and arrangers and is still a major player in today’s classic jazz scene. Born in New York City in 1914, he first came to prominence in 1935 with the Bob Crosby Orchestra. His bass playing and writing skills were a major contribution to the success of the Crosby group and his composition for bass and drums, “Big Noise from Winnetka” became a signature tune for the band.
Haggart later co-led the World’s Greatest Jazz Band, worked in the radio and jingle market and wrote some enduring standards, including “What’s New.”
He continues to appear at jazz festivals and parties and lends his arranging skills to such projects as Kenny Davern’s album with strings, “My Inspiration.”
Bob was interviewed on September 22, 1995 at Hamilton College by Dr.
Michael Woods. Pianist Ralph Sutton was also present at the interview.
The Hamilton College Jazz Archive are filming interviews with some of America’s greatest jazz musicians. We’re fortunate to have with us today Bob Haggart. Pleased to be with you.
